insights.title: Rain is more than crops can use
insights.body: Rain exceeds crop water demand by about 2288 mm a year. Waterlogging and runoff are bigger risks than drought.

insights.title: Fields are greenest in October, barest in February
insights.body: Satellite greenness of the farmland here peaks at 0.70 and drops to 0.60 (0 = bare, 1 = dense crop). The low months are when soil is most exposed to rain and wind.

insights.title: Best-matched crops for this area
insights.body: Rubber, Oil palm and Cashew score highest on climate, water and soil fit.

outlook.method: Theil-Sen trend + Mann-Kendall test on 2001-2024 yearly data, extended to 2035 with an 80% prediction range. Where there is no clear trend, the 2001-2024 average is projected. Statistical extrapolation, not a climate-model forecast.

consequences.headline: +0.7 °C warmer on average by 2035
consequences.detail: The yearly average moves from 27.6 °C to about 28.3 °C. That is close to the top of the comfortable range for Chickpea.
consequences.action: Watch heat stress in cool-climate crops; earlier sowing helps.

consequences.headline: In a dry year, rain can drop to about 2,606 mm
consequences.detail: That is 17% below the 3,153 mm average; about 1 year in 10 is this dry or worse.
consequences.action: Keep a drought-tolerant crop in the plan as insurance.
